questions.q: What is the recommended starting point in this lesson's decision framework, before considering Managed Instance or a VM?
options: Azure SQL Database — you move up a tier only when a specific, named requirement forces it
SQL Server on an Azure VM, since it has the most features
Azure SQL Managed Instance, since it's a middle ground
Whichever option is cheapest that month
questions.explain: Most new workloads stop at Azure SQL Database. You move up only when a concrete requirement forces it, not out of general caution.

questions.q: Which of these is a real signal that forces Azure SQL Managed Instance instead of Azure SQL Database?
options: The application depends on SQL Server Agent jobs or cross-database queries/transactions within one instance
The team simply prefers a bigger-sounding product name
The database has more than 10 tables
The application uses SELECT statements
questions.explain: Agent jobs and cross-database queries rely on instance-level features Azure SQL Database doesn't provide, which is exactly the kind of concrete requirement that forces the next tier.

questions.q: Which of these is a real signal that forces SQL Server on an Azure VM instead of Managed Instance?
options: You need OS-level access to install third-party software, or a specific SQL Server version/feature Managed Instance doesn't offer
You want Microsoft to manage patching for you
The database is small
You want to avoid ever thinking about infrastructure again
questions.explain: OS-level access and unsupported version/feature requirements are the concrete forcing functions for a VM — and both come with the cost of now owning patching yourself.

questions.q: What's the real cost of choosing a VM to get OS-level control, according to this lesson (tying back to Lessons 4 and 13)?
options: You now own OS patching, SQL Server patching, and HA/DR infrastructure yourself — none of it is managed for you anymore
There is no cost — a VM is strictly better in every way
VMs are always cheaper than Managed Instance
A VM automatically handles all backups with zero configuration
questions.explain: The control a VM gives you is exactly the control you now have to exercise yourself — patching, HA/DR, and OS configuration all become your responsibility.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is "it depends" a legitimate answer when choosing between the three deployment options, rather than a dodge?
options: Because the right choice is decided by matching specific, named business requirements against each tier's real constraints, not by picking a favorite
Because there's no way to ever make this decision correctly
Because all three options are functionally identical
Because the decision should be made randomly
questions.explain: The whole point of the framework is that the decision is defensible: it's driven by concrete requirements, and different requirements genuinely lead to different correct answers.
